source: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Breast Cancer
recommendations: Refer to breast specialist / genetic counselor if high risk or family history suggests hereditary cancer syndrome
Recommend annual mammogram screening, starting at age 40 or 10 years earlier than the youngest affected first-degree relative
Discuss risk reduction strategies: chemoprevention (e.g., tamoxifen, raloxifene, or aromatase inhibitors) if appropriate
Advise lifestyle changes: weight control, regular exercise, limiting alcohol intake

follow_up.action: Refer to breast health clinic for risk assessment and clinical breast exam
Screening mammography and clinical breast exam
Discuss genetic testing results (if performed) and implications for family members

contraindications.condition: History of deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, or active pregnancy

emergency_signs: Breast cancer red flags: new breast lump, skin dimpling, nipple retraction, bloody nipple discharge, localized breast pain
references: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Breast Cancer, Version 1.2024
